notes: §1985:VI.5.9.4 GR3: 'Its PICTURE character-string can contain only the symbols '9', 'P', 'S', and 'V'. The number of digit positions that can be described by the PICTURE character-string must range from 1 to 18 inclusive'. AnalyzeCharacterString's last arm makes a string of 9 P S V category Numeric and counts its digit positions as the 9s plus every P (DigitPositions); DataBinder.BindEntry passes each written PICTURE to ScreenPictureDigitCapacity, and EditionContext.CheckDigitCapacity refuses fewer than 1 and more than MaxDigits, which EditionInfo.MaxDigits makes 18 below 2002 (COBOL0802) and 31 from 2002. The lower bound is also PictureComposition.Validate's refusal of a string with no 9 (COBOL1934). Probed at --std 85: PIC 9(18), S9(18), 9(16)PP and PP9(16) compile; PIC 9(19), 9(17)PP, PP9(17) and S9(18)V9 are refused with COBOL0802, PIC S, V and PPP with COBOL1934. Sentence b, the content with an operational sign, is carried by the SIGN clause's representation (S9(18) VALUE -1 displays -000000000000000001). The witness stores and displays 18-digit, 16V2 and 1-digit items.

next.reason: 1985: a numeric PICTURE contains only '9', 'P', 'S', 'V' and 'The number of digit positions ... must range from 1 to 18 inclusive'; content numeric characters plus an operational sign if signed. 2023: §2023:13.18.40.4 GR11 (at least one '9', may contain 'P', 'S', 'V') and §2023:13.18.40.4 GR14 ('9' 'shall contain a numeric character in the range 0 through 9 with the possible inclusion of an operational sign') keep the symbol set and content, but §2023:13.18.40.3 SR14 sets 'from 1 through 31' digit positions: 19 to 31 digit numeric PICTUREs refused in 1985 are accepted.
